payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Astrid, Gillian, Reanna, Stefania

payload.content: Hi all — Stefania here. My skill is security:0.94 and my private costs are heavily skewed: ISSUE-0002 tasks are cheap for me (review=1.75, test=2.45, implement=3.50) while all ISSUE-0001 tasks are very expensive (24–60). So I plan to claim one of the ISSUE-0002 micro-tasks. My first preference is ISSUE-0002::review (cost 1.75), then ::test, then ::implement. Please tell me if you also need an ISSUE-0002 slot so we can avoid duplicates. If someone else strongly wants ::review, I can take ::test instead.

Additional thought for the group: there are 4 agents and 8 micro-tasks, so we can complete at most 4. To maximize the joint score, we want 4 DISTINCT feasible claims. The 5 ISSUE-0001 (critical) tasks are the highest priority; the 3 ISSUE-0002 (medium) tasks are lower priority but cheaper for me. My proposal: those of you with api-development skill should cover the ORDER-0001 critical tasks (implement/review/test/docs/triage) since my costs there are 24–60 (infeasible-ish). I will take an ISSUE-0002 slot so I don't waste a critical slot. Unless I hear a strong objection, I will claim ISSUE-0002::review, falling back to ::test. Please post your planned claims so we avoid duplicates.

Hi all — Reanna here. My skills: api-development:0.98, ui-ux-design:0.90, availability 6.0h. My private costs strongly favor the critical ISSUE-0001 tasks: triage=2.22, review=2.78, docs=2.78, test=3.89, implement=5.55. My ISSUE-0002 costs are also low (review=1.82, test=2.55, implement=3.64) but those are only medium priority.

Plan: since I have the strongest api-development fit, I will claim a CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 task. My preference order: ISSUE-0001::triage (cost 2.22) > ::review (2.78) > ::docs (2.78) > ::test (3.89) > ::implement (5.55).

Proposal for a distinct 4-claim set maximizing priority: Stefania takes ISSUE-0002::review (her cheapest, medium). Astrid and Gillian each take a different critical ISSUE-0001 micro-task (e.g. ::implement, ::review, ::docs, ::test). I'll take ISSUE-0001::triage unless someone else needs it — if so, I can flex to ::review or ::docs. Please post your planned claims so we avoid duplicates. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Reanna: confirming my final claim for execution — ISSUE-0001::triage (cost 2.22, effort 2.4, critical, api-development). If any of Astrid/Gillian need ::triage specifically, message me and I'll flex to ISSUE-0001::review or ::docs. Otherwise I'm committing to ::triage. This leaves ::implement, ::review, ::docs, ::test for the other three, plus ISSUE-0002::review for Stefania. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Gillian here. My skills are ui-ux-design:0.87 and security:0.71, so ISSUE-0002 (tags ui-ux-design/security) is cheap for me and ISSUE-0001 (api-development) is very expensive: ISSUE-0002 costs = review 1.12, test 1.57, implement 2.24; ISSUE-0001 costs = triage 24, review 30, docs 30, test 42, implement 60.

Plan: I will claim ISSUE-0002::test (cost 1.57). This lets Stefania take ISSUE-0002::review (her first preference, cost 1.75) with no duplicate — and the pair (Stefania::review + Gillian::test) is the cheapest split of the two medium slots (1.75+1.57=3.32 < 1.12+2.45).

Reanna is on ISSUE-0001::triage. Astrid — you're the remaining agent; please claim a CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 micro-task (::review, ::docs, ::test, or ::implement) to maximize priority_sum. That yields 4 distinct claims: 2 critical + 2 medium. Final: Gillian -> ISSUE-0002::test.

Stefania: confirming my final claim for execution — ISSUE-0002::review (cost 1.75, effort 1.0, medium, tags [ui-ux-design, security]). Gillian takes ISSUE-0002::test, Reanna takes ISSUE-0001::triage. That gives 4 distinct claims: 2 critical (Reanna::triage + Astrid's critical pick) + 2 medium (me::review + Gillian::test). Astrid, please claim a distinct CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 micro-task (::review, ::docs, ::test, or ::implement) — avoid ::triage (Reanna). No duplicates. I'm committing to ISSUE-0002::review.

Reanna: Final plan locked from my side. Distinct 4-claim set: Reanna -> ISSUE-0001::triage (critical, cost 2.22); Stefania -> ISSUE-0002::review (medium); Gillian -> ISSUE-0002::test (medium); Astrid -> one CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 micro-task of your choice among ::review / ::docs / ::test / ::implement (avoid ::triage). This yields 2 critical + 2 medium, no duplicates. I'm committing to ISSUE-0001::triage in execution. Astrid, please post your pick so we stay conflict-free.

Gillian: Confirming final claim — I will take ISSUE-0002::test (cost 1.57, effort 1.4, medium, tags [ui-ux-design, security]). This keeps the cheapest split of the two medium slots: Stefania::review (1.75) + Gillian::test (1.57) = 3.32, better than swapping. Reanna is on ISSUE-0001::triage. Astrid — please claim a distinct CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 micro-task (::review / ::docs / ::test / ::implement), avoiding ::triage. That gives 4 distinct claims: 2 critical + 2 medium, no duplicates. Locking in Gillian -> ISSUE-0002::test.

Stefania: Plan is aligned. Locking my claim — Stefania -> ISSUE-0002::review (cost 1.75, effort 1.0, medium, tags [ui-ux-design, security]). Full distinct 4-claim set: Stefania::ISSUE-0002::review, Gillian::ISSUE-0002::test, Reanna::ISSUE-0001::triage, Astrid::one CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 (::review/::docs/::test/::implement, avoid ::triage). Astrid — please confirm your critical pick so we stay conflict-free and avoid a random fill/violation. I will commit ISSUE-0002::review in execution.

Reanna: Acknowledged — plan is aligned and locked. Reanna -> ISSUE-0001::triage (critical, cost 2.22). Stefania -> ISSUE-0002::review, Gillian -> ISSUE-0002::test, Astrid -> any CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 (::review/::docs/::test/::implement, avoid ::triage). Astrid, please confirm your pick. I will commit ISSUE-0001::triage in execution. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Gillian: My plan is unchanged and locked. I will claim ISSUE-0002::test (cost 1.57, effort 1.4, medium, tags [ui-ux-design, security]). Rationale: my ISSUE-0001 (api-development) costs are 24–60, so critical tasks are far too expensive for me; ISSUE-0002 is my strength. Keeping Stefania on ::review (1.75) + me on ::test (1.57) = 3.32 is cheaper than the swap (1.12+2.45=3.57). Astrid — please confirm a distinct CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 micro-task (::review/::docs/::test/::implement, avoid ::triage taken by Reanna) so we land 4 distinct claims with no duplicates. Committing Gillian -> ISSUE-0002::test in execution.

Stefania: Final confirmation. My claim is locked: Stefania -> ISSUE-0002::review (cost 1.75, effort 1.0, medium, tags [ui-ux-design, security]). Agreed distinct 4-claim set: Stefania::ISSUE-0002::review, Gillian::ISSUE-0002::test, Reanna::ISSUE-0001::triage, Astrid::one CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 (::review/::docs/::test/::implement — avoid ::triage). Astrid, please post your critical pick ASAP so we get 4 distinct feasible claims and avoid a random fill/violation. I will commit ISSUE-0002::review in execution. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Reanna: Locked and ready. My claim: ISSUE-0001::triage (critical, cost 2.22). Agreed distinct set: Reanna::ISSUE-0001::triage, Stefania::ISSUE-0002::review, Gillian::ISSUE-0002::test, Astrid::one CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 (::review/::docs/::test/::implement — avoid ::triage). Astrid, please confirm your pick. I will commit ISSUE-0001::triage in execution.

Gillian: Final planning confirmation. My claim is locked: Gillian -> ISSUE-0002::test (cost 1.57, effort 1.4, medium, tags [ui-ux-design, security]). Agreed distinct 4-claim set: Gillian::ISSUE-0002::test, Stefania::ISSUE-0002::review (1.75), Reanna::ISSUE-0001::triage, Astrid::one CRITICAL ISSUE-0001 (::review/::docs/::test/::implement — avoid ::triage). This keeps the cheapest split of the two medium slots (1.75+1.57=3.32 < 1.12+2.45=3.57). Astrid, please confirm your critical pick. I will commit ISSUE-0002::test in execution.
